F. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS

   CITY OF INGLEWOOD

  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A

  MARCH 2024 MEETING MINUTES

A. OPENING CEREMONIES
 Chairperson Hibler welcomed the commission and the public for their attendance and participation.
 Meeting was held at 7:05 pm (PST) in the Community Room A located in the first floor on 02/28/24
 Attendees included Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett C.S. Roberts, Lois Hale, Peter
  Puglese, and William Thompson.
 Miss Katrina Gamez acted as Secretary to assist and attend the Parking and Traffic Commission.

B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEM
 None

C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1. Approval of the Minutes for the Meeting held on February 28th, 2024
 A motion to accept the meeting notes was made by Richard Galindo and seconded by Kip Rudd.
 The motion was carried by the following roll call vote: Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd,
  Brett Roberts and Lois Hale. All commissioners approved the minutes of the meeting notes. There
  was no rejection or noes.

D. PUBLIC HEARING
1. None
 Staff report recommending that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to
  receive public comments regarding the termination of the Residential Permit Parking Program on
  117th Street from Dehn Avenue and Lemoli Avenue within District 11; and provide direction to the
  City Engineer on how to proceed was withdrawn from the March Traffic and Parking Commission
  agenda.

E. UNFINISHED BUSINESS
1. City-owned parking facilities as parking meter zones with special event parking rates and fines
a. The staff report can be obtained at
  HTTPS://WWW.CITYOFINGLEWOOD.ORG/AGENDACENTER/VIEWFILE/ITEM/16627?FILEID=23655
  Oral status report on the implementation plan for event parking rates and fines at public parking
  facilities and a timeline on when a draft plan will be completed for Commission review and comment.
 No Update at this time. Commissioners will follow this issue and ask questions when necessary.

2. Performance reports for the parking and shuttle service utilizing city-owned parking facilities
a. A shuttle performance report for the September-December 2023 NFL season and the latest
  quarterly report that would include other events that utilized the shuttle system.
 William Thomson recommended visiting https://inglewoodparkgo.com to become familiar with using
  the shuttle. Commissioners will follow this issue and ask questions when necessary.

F. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

 The resident of 117th Street made the following comments.
   There is no enforcement for speeding vehichles.
   The parking program does not support personal events and parties.
   The parking program is against providing a greater number of permits available per household.
   Others favor the parking program because of the accessibility of street parking to residents and
  visitors.

G. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
1. The members of the Parking and Traffic Commission will provide oral reports, including reports on
  City related travels where lodging expenses are incurred, and/or address any matters they deem of
  general interest to the public.
 Commissioners thanked William Thompson and crew for helping direct traffic during the noisy event.
 Commissioners asked about the timing of the traffic signal lights on Florence Avenue and High
  Street and High Street and Redondo Blvd. It was responded that the timing cannot be changed due
  to Metro Light Rail.
 Comissioners asked about no left turn signal from West Blvd onto Florence Avenue. It was
  responded that this is not a light controlled by City Of Inglewood. It is a light owned by City of LA.
  Public Works staff stated that the City of Los Angeles will be contacted regarding signal timing and
  informed of the issue.
 Comissioners asked about signal traffic timing on Century Blvd and Crenshaw Blvd. They were
  informed that due to construction, signal timings have been adjusted.

H. ANNOUNCEMENTS
1. It was announced that the next Traffic and Parking Commission meeting will be Wednesday, April
  24, 2024 at 7:00 p.m. m., 1st Floor, City Hall Community Room A, Inglewood City Hall One
  Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood, CA 90301

I. ADJOURNMENT
1. The Parking and Traffic Commission meeting ended at 7:37 PM PST.

J. ATTACHMENT
1. Attendance Sheet
2. Street Closure Message

 The first motion to accept was made by Kip Rudd and seconded by Richard Galindo

 Commissioner Kip Rudd asked that the matter come before the Commission for review and

1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City

 The resident of Crenshaw Boulevard made the following comments.
 Parking in the alley located between 108th and 111th Streets on Crenshaw Boulevard is not
  permitted. The resident asked the reason for the non-permission and the parking citation. It was
  explained to the resident that it is in the City's Municipal Code and that no sign is necessary for
  compliance. It is recommended that the resident visit the Los Angeles County Assessor to verify
  property and alley boundaries. For additional information, the ordinance can be found in Chapter
  3, Article 2, Section 3-50 of the City Municipal Code. It says § 3-50 (Parking in Alleys Prohibited)
  that “it shall be unlawful for any person to stop, stand or park a vehicle in any alley.”
 The alley located at 117th Street and Crenshaw Boulevard has not been swept according to the
  resident. The resident was advised to contact the Public Works Office for quick response and
  reporting. The appropriate person within Public Works can be connected to help directly and
  effectively.

G. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
1. The members of the Parking and Traffic Commission will provide oral reports, including reports on
  City related travels where lodging expenses are incurred, and/or address any matters they deem of
  general interest to the public.
 The commissioners thanked everyone who helped them through their community activities, as well
  as those who attended the meeting.
 Commissioner Rudd asked about Google Green Light and asked if it is a good tool for the City to
  use. As information, Green Light optimizes traffic lights to reduce vehicle emissions in cities, helping
  mitigate climate change and improving urban mobility. City staff responded that it is too early to
  determine the need to invest in such tool.

DATE:  Wednesday, May 22, 2024

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Adoption of Resolution Recommending Termination of Residential Permit
  Parking Program for 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street

RECOMMENDATION:
It is requested that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the information included in this
report and approve the resolution recommending that the City Council adopt an ordinance to
terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program within District 9 on 6th Avenue from 104th
Street to 108th Street.

BACKGROUND:
On June 16, 2020, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 20-90 to implement a Citywide Permit
Parking Districts Program to cover all streets within the Permit Parking Districts map
accompanying the Ordinance. The program is designed to reduce traffic and parking impacts
to residential neighborhoods by non-resident vehicles parking in the area while attending events
at the City’s venues. The Ordinance grants the Public Works Director the authority to determine
whether permit parking restrictions apply 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, or any portion thereof.
The City must post signs of the permit parking restrictions.

Inglewood Municipal Code section 3-76 & 3-76.1 provide that residents and/or business persons
in a neighborhood may petition for the termination of a Permit Parking District by submitting a
petition bearing the signatures of at least 10 adults from different households and/or businesses.

On October 10, 2023, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the removal
of Residential Permit Parking on 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9.
There is a count of thirty-eight (38) properties that are within the boundary. Ten (10) valid
signatures (one signature per residential unit) were submitted on the petition.

Accordingly, on February 5, 2024, a notice was sent to all addresses within the petition boundary
to attend the February Traffic and Parking Commission meeting to express their views on the
matter.

DISCUSSION:
On February 28, 2024, the Parking and Traffic Commission held a public hearing on the issue
of terminating the Residential Permit Parking Program for 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th
Street within District 9. The Parking and Traffic Commission listened to public comments and
all district commissioners voted to approve the request to send questionairres to addresses in
the affected district.

On March 8, 2024, the Public Works Department mailed questionaries to each resident residing
in the boundary area of the petition and requested the questionnaires be returned within thirty

(30) calendar days. For the parking restrictions to be removed, a minimum of seventy-five
percent (75%) of the returned questionnaires must be in favor of the removal (IMC § 3-76(a)).

On April 17, 2024, the questionnaires were counted. The City received twenty-nine (29) votes,
with twenty-seven (27) votes cast to approve the termination and two (2) votes opposed the
termination of the Residential Permit Parking Program, i.e., ninety-three percent (93%) of
households supported the removal of 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street from Permit
Parking District 9.

Based on the results, Public Works staff recommends that the Parking and Traffic Commission
approve the resolution recommending that the City Council adopt an ordinance terminating the
Residential Permit Parking Program for 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within
District 9.

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Termination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
residential permit parking within District 9 on 6th Avenue between 108th Street and 104th Street. Per
Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the Inglewood
Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday February 28, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses within the subject area. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the subject area listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some
on-street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a
nearby commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking is severely impacted and if the termination of a residential permit parking within District
9 on 6th Avenue between 108th Street and 104th Street would be warranted. If it is determined to be
warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the subject area.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is terminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will
not be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you
have any questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the
public hearing, please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  AVISO DE AUDIENCIA PÚBLICA
  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de
  Estacionamiento en la Zona Residencial
Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la
terminación del permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 6th Avenue entre 108th
Street y 104th Street. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood,
este asunto se presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar
especificados:

  Miércoles 28 de Febrero de 2024 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones dentro del área de asunto. Cualquier persona
interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es dar a todos los residentes del área mencionada anteriormente
la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema.

El propósito del Programa de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad
para los residentes de algunos espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un
vecindario donde los clientes y/o empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan
todos los espacios de estacionamiento disponibles en la calle. La Comisión de Tráfico y
Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de estacionamiento en la
calle se ve gravemente afectada y si se justificaría la terminación de un permiso de estacionamiento
residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 6th Avenue entre 108th Street y 104th Street. Si se determina que
está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar dentro del área en cuestión.

Si se rescinde un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no todos los residentes y
visitantes de este vecindario tendrán restricciones para estacionar en las calles públicas en cualquier
momento; incluso durante eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea
expresar una opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento
de Obras Públicas de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.

Date:  March 8, 2024

To:  Residents of 6th Avenue

Subject:  Vote to Approve OR Reject the termination of Residential Permit Parking on 6th
  Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9

The purpose of this letter is to allow residents the opportunity to vote on the removal of the residential
permit parking on 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9.

By voting "approve", this street will not be subject to the rules of a Residential Permit Parking District.
By voting "reject", this street will continue to have permit parking and follow the rules associated with it.
The complete rules and procedures can be found in the Inglewood Municipal Code Section 3-76
(Establishment of a Permit Parking District) through Section 3-76.1 (Amending or Terminating a Permit
Parking District).

Since the Parking and Traffic Commission has determined that permitted parking may not be warranted
in the area in question, ballots are mailed to all residences within the boundary of the subject street.

If seventy-five percent (75%) or more of the returned ballots vote “approve” for the termination of
residential permit parking, then an ordinance amending the Residential Permit Parking District will be
submitted to the City Council for consideration. If approved, on 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th
Street within District 9 will not be subject to the Residential Permit Parking District rules. Therefore, all
vehicles can park on these streets without showing a parking permit at all hours of the day, every day of
the week. Additionally, the current parking prohibitions for street sweeping will remain unchanged.

Using the enclosed ballot, please vote to approve or reject the termination of the residential permit
parking on 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9. Please return the ballot to the
City of Inglewood Public Works Department by April 12, 2024. Only one vote per household will be
accepted. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to get in touch with the Public Works
Department, at (310) 412-5333.

Yours Truly,

El propósito de esta carta es brindarles a los residentes la oportunidad de votar sobre la eliminación
del permiso de estacionamiento residencial en la 6th Avenue desde la 104th Street hasta la 108th
Street dentro del Distrito 9

Al votar "aprobar", esta calle no estará sujeta a las normas de un distrito de estacionamiento con
permiso residencial. Al votar "rechazar", esta calle seguirá teniendo permiso de estacionamiento y
seguirá las reglas asociadas a la misma. Las reglas y procedimientos completos se pueden
encontrar en el Código Municipal de Inglewood, Sección 3-76 (Establecimiento de un Distrito de
Estacionamiento con Permiso) hasta la Sección 3-76.1 (Modificación o Terminación de un Distrito
de Estacionamiento con Permiso).

Dado que la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico ha determinado que es posible que el
estacionamiento permitido no esté garantizado en el área en cuestión, las boletas se envían por
correo a todas las residencias dentro de los límites de la calle en cuestión. Si el setenta y cinco por
ciento (75%) o más de las boletas devueltas votan "aprobar" la terminación del permiso de
estacionamiento residencial, entonces se presentará al Concejo Municipal para su consideración
una ordenanza que modifica el Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial.

Si se aprueba, en la 6th Avenue desde la 104th Street hasta la 108th Street dentro del Distrito 9 no
estará sujeto a las reglas del Distrito con Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial. Por lo tanto,
todos los vehículos pueden estacionar en estas calles sin mostrar un permiso de estacionamiento a
todas horas del día, todos los días de la semana. Además, las prohibiciones de estacionamiento
actuales para el barrido de calles se mantendrán sin cambios.

Usando la boleta adjunta, vote para aprobar o rechazar la terminación del permiso de
estacionamiento residencial en la 6th Avenue desde la 104th Street hasta la 108th Street dentro del
Distrito 9. Por favor devuelva la boleta al Departamento de Obras Públicas de la Ciudad de
Inglewood antes del 12 de Abril de 2024. Sólo se aceptará un voto por hogar. Si tiene alguna
pregunta, no dude en comunicarse con el Departamento de Obras Públicas al (310) 412-5333.
